chunks: And by his chain, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
If an animal limb is gifted to me, I would accept it.

key_terms.كُرَاعٌ: A cut of meat or animal limb, often used as a term for a gift of food

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about accepting gifts of food or animal parts?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi underscores the Prophetic etiquette of accepting gifts to strengthen social bonds, with 'kura' referring to a specific cut of meat or animal limb, illustrating that even modest offerings are valued. In Shia tradition, this act is seen as a means of fostering love (mawaddah) and reciprocity among the community, reflecting the broader Islamic principle that gifts do not increase wealth but rather increase affection. The acceptance of such gifts also serves as a practical demonstration of humility and approachability for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

en.hubeali:
And by his chain, 
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘
If an animal limb is gifted to me<sup>asws</sup>, I<sup>saww</sup> would accept it’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy, , who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘
Of a believer’s upholding the honor of his Muslim brother is to accept his gifts and present him a gift of whatever is possible for him without over-burdening himself.’”
